name: Flowsery
description: Query Flowsery's privacy-first, cookie-free web analytics: live visitors, traffic breakdowns by 25 dimensions, goals, revenue, visitor journeys, and the bugs Flowsery's AI found in session recordings. Sign in with OAuth or an API key.
author: Flowsery

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.title: List Workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces this sign-in can act in, across every organization the user belongs to. Returns { status, data } with one entry per workspace: id, name, organization { id, name }, role { key, name }, permissions, isDefault and current. Call this when the user names a workspace, client or organization, or when data they expect is missing, then pass the matching id as workspaceId to every other tool. Without workspaceId, tools act in the workspace marked current. A workspace API token (flow_ws_) belongs to one workspace, so it lists only that one; a website key (flow_) belongs to one website and fails with a 400 here. Takes no arguments.

id.description: Pass as workspaceId to other tools

current.description: True for the workspace this call ran in

tools.name: list_websites
tools.title: List Websites
tools.description: List the websites the current API token can read, with id, domain, timezone, currency, and KPI goal per site. A workspace token (flow_ws_) returns every website in the workspace; a website key (flow_) returns only its own. Call this first with a workspace token: every other tool then needs websiteId or domain from this list, and omitting both fails with 'Website ID or domain is required'. Takes no parameters. Use get_metadata instead when you already know the website and only need its settings.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to use the default workspace. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace do not exist in another

id.description: Pass as websiteId to other tools

kpi.description: Goal name used as the website's KPI

tools.name: get_metadata
tools.title: Get Website Settings
tools.description: Get one website's settings: domain, timezone, currency, KPI goal name, logo, and color scheme. Read-only; nothing is changed. Call it after list_websites to learn the timezone and currency before running date-range reports, then pass that timezone to the report tools. With a workspace token pass websiteId or domain; with neither it returns the same website list as list_websites, so prefer list_websites for discovery. A website key needs no selector.

domain.description: Website domain from list_websites (e.g. "example.com"). Alternative to websiteId with a workspace token.

id.description: Pass as websiteId to other tools

tools.name: get_overview
tools.title: Get Traffic Overview
tools.description: Get headline totals for one website over a date range as a single row: visitors, sessions, bounce rate, average session duration, revenue, revenue per visitor, and conversion rate. Dates default to the last 30 days ending now; timezone defaults to the site setting. Every filter_* argument narrows the whole result, so filter_country plus filter_device answers 'mobile visitors from Germany' in one call. Use get_timeseries for the trend over time and a get_* breakdown tool for the split by page, source, or geography. Requires websiteId or domain with a workspace token.

tools.name: get_realtime
tools.title: Get Active Visitor Count
tools.description: Count the visitors active on the site within the last 5 minutes. A point-in-time number with no history: it takes no date, filter, or pagination arguments. Use get_timeseries with interval hour for recent trends and get_realtime_map when you need where those visitors are. Returns data[0].visitors. Poll no more than once every 5 seconds. Requires websiteId or domain with a workspace token.

tools.name: get_realtime_map
tools.title: Get Live Visitor Map
tools.description: Get the visitors active on the user's own website in the last 5 minutes with their approximate city-level location, for a live map view. Coordinates are rounded to 0.1 degrees, and no IP addresses or other identifying details are returned. Use get_realtime when only the count matters, and get_countries or get_cities for geography over a historical date range. Takes only the website selector: no dates, filters, or pagination. tools.title: List Detected Issues
tools.description: List issues the AI found while analyzing session recordings: bugs, broken flows, and UX problems, deduplicated across sessions and ranked by severity (or by last seen with sort recency). Each row has title, severity, status, sessions affected, and first/last seen; the response also carries site-wide open, in_progress, and resolved counts plus pagination.total. Start here for 'what is broken', then call get_issue with an id for occurrences, steps to replicate, and comments. Suspended issues are hidden unless status is suspended, so an issue that vanished was probably suspended, not deleted. On a free trial only the first 10 issues are listed and counted. Requires websiteId or domain with a workspace token.

websiteId.description: Website ID from list_websites. Required with a workspace token unless domain is given; ignored with a website key.

domain.description: Website domain from list_websites (e.g. "example.com"). Alternative to websiteId with a workspace token.

status.description: Only list issues in this workflow state: open is new and untriaged, in_progress is being worked on, resolved was marked fixed, suspended was hidden as a known non-problem. Omit to list open, in_progress and resolved together; suspended issues appear only with status suspended.

severity.description: Only list issues at this severity, as rated by the AI that found them. Omit to include every severity.

search.description: Words to look for in issue titles and descriptions, e.g. "checkout"

sort.description: severity puts the most severe issues first; recency puts the most recently seen first. Omit to sort by severity.

limit.description: Page size: how many issues to return in this call. Omit for 100.

offset.description: How many issues to skip, for reading the next page. Omit to start at the first one.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to use the default workspace. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace do not exist in another

id.description: Pass as issueId to get_issue or update_issue_status

sessionsCount.description: Analyzed sessions that hit this issue

counts.description: Issue counts by status for the whole website, ignoring filters

total.description: Rows matching the query before paging

tools.name: get_issue
tools.title: Get Issue Detail
tools.description: Get full detail for one AI-detected issue: every occurrence with timestamps, the sessions behind it, steps to replicate, comments, and any linked Linear or Jira ticket. Get issueId from list_issues; use this only when you need the evidence behind one issue. An unknown id, or one from another website, fails with 'Issue not found'; on a free trial only the first 10 issues are available, and later ones fail as not included in the current plan. Each session lists its recording id, the anonymous visitorUid, start URL and page title, timing and event counts; no names, emails or locations are returned, so surface only what answers the question. Requires websiteId or domain with a workspace token.

tools.name: update_issue_status
tools.title: Update Issue Status
tools.description: Set an issue's status to open, in_progress, resolved, or suspended and return the updated issue. Only the status changes; title, severity, occurrences, and comments stay, and any status can be set again later, so this is reversible. Confirm which state the user means before calling: resolved asserts the bug is fixed, suspended hides a known non-problem from the default list_issues result. Not a delete: issues cannot be removed through this server. Get issueId from list_issues; an unknown id fails with 'Issue not found', and on a free trial issues beyond the first 10 fail as not included in the current plan. Requires websiteId or domain with a workspace token.

tools.name: track_goal
tools.title: Track Goal Event
tools.description: Record one completion of a custom goal. The goal is created on first use, so no setup call is needed. Pass visitorUid (the anonymous visitor ID Flowsery assigned on the user's own website) so the completion attaches to that visitor's sessions and source; omit it for an anonymous completion. Each call appends a completion, so repeating it counts the goal twice. Use track_payment for revenue, which records a payment goal on its own. Undo with delete_goals. Requires websiteId or domain with a workspace token.

websiteId.description: Website ID from list_websites. Required with a workspace token unless domain is given; ignored with a website key.

domain.description: Website domain from list_websites (e.g. "example.com"). Alternative to websiteId with a workspace token.

name.description: Which goal was completed, e.g. "newsletter_signup" or "add-to-cart". Reuse the exact name for repeat completions: get_goals, filter_goal and delete_goals all match on it.

visitorUid.description: Anonymous visitor ID Flowsery assigned on the user's own website (the _fs_vid value). Omit to record an anonymous completion.

sessionUid.description: Session ID of the visitor's current session (the _fs_sid value). Ties the completion to that session; without it a server-side call uses the visitor's latest active session.

timezone.description: The visitor's IANA timezone (e.g. "Europe/Berlin"). Helps place the visitor in a country when the call comes from a server or proxy.

metadata.description: Extra context saved with this completion, such as { "plan": "pro", "source": "footer" }. At most 10 keys; omit when there is nothing to add.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to use the default workspace. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace do not exist in another

data.description: One confirmation message. The completion is written asynchronously and shows in get_goals shortly after

tools.name: delete_goals
tools.title: Delete Goal Events
tools.description: Permanently delete recorded goal completions matching every filter given (filters combine with AND). At least one of visitorId, name, startAt, or endAt is required or the call fails before reaching the API; startAt and endAt are independent, so one bound alone is allowed. Without a date range, matches are deleted across the whole history. Returns the number of rows deleted. Cannot be undone: restate website, filters, and range and get explicit confirmation first. Deletes completions only; the goal definition stays and get_goals still lists it. Use delete_payments for revenue records and update_issue_status for issues. Requires websiteId or domain with a workspace token.

websiteId.description: Website ID from list_websites. Required with a workspace token unless domain is given; ignored with a website key.

domain.description: Website domain from list_websites (e.g. "example.com"). Alternative to websiteId with a workspace token.

visitorId.description: Delete completions of this visitor (the id get_visitor takes). Combined with the other filters using AND.

name.description: Delete completions of this goal name (as listed by get_goals)

startAt.description: ISO 8601 start of the deletion window, inclusive (e.g. "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"). May be used without endAt.

endAt.description: ISO 8601 end of the deletion window, inclusive (e.g. "2026-01-31T23:59:59Z"). May be used without startAt.

tools.name: track_payment
tools.title: Track Payment
tools.description: Record an analytics payment; this never charges a customer, moves money, or issues a refund. Revenue appears in get_overview, get_timeseries, every breakdown's revenue column, and the visitor profile. Skip it when the site's provider (Stripe, LemonSqueezy, Polar, and other connected providers) is tracked automatically, or the revenue is counted twice; use track_goal for conversions without revenue. transactionId must be unique: a repeated id is rejected, not deduplicated. A new payment also records a payment goal completion (free_trial when amount is 0); isRenewal skips that. isRefund with an existing transactionId overwrites that payment's recorded refund amount and any supplied customer attribution instead of adding a row. Attribution looks up a known visitor by visitorUid, customerId, or email; with no match the revenue is kept but its source shows as Unknown. Send email and name only when the user supplied them and wants the payment attributed. Undo with delete_payments. Requires websiteId or domain with a workspace token.

websiteId.description: Website ID from list_websites. Required with a workspace token unless domain is given; ignored with a website key.

domain.description: Website domain from list_websites (e.g. "example.com"). Alternative to websiteId with a workspace token.

amount.description: Payment amount in major currency units (e.g. 29.99). With isRefund, the amount refunded. 0 records a free_trial goal instead of a payment goal.

transactionId.description: Unique transaction ID from the payment provider. Must not repeat across payments; reuse it only with isRefund to mark that payment refunded.

visitorUid.description: Anonymous visitor ID Flowsery assigned on the user's own website (the _fs_vid value). Without it, or a customerId or email matching a known visitor, the payment is attributed to Unknown.

sessionUid.description: Session ID of the visitor's current session (the _fs_sid value), so the payment is tied to that session

timezone.description: The visitor's IANA timezone (e.g. "Europe/Berlin"). Helps place the visitor in a country when the call comes from a server or proxy.

email.description: Customer email, used only to attribute the payment to a known visitor

name.description: Customer name shown on the payment

customerId.description: Customer ID from the payment provider. Also used to find the visitor when visitorUid is absent.

isRenewal.description: True for recurring or renewal charges. Renewals count in revenue but do not record the automatic payment goal.

isRefund.description: True to record a refund that already happened. With an existing transactionId, marks that payment refunded by amount instead of creating a new record.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 time the payment happened (e.g. "2026-01-15T10:30:00Z"), for backfilling. Defaults to now.

customerIp.description: The buyer's IP address at checkout, for a server-side call that cannot match the payment to a visitor. Flowsery keeps only the country it resolves from it.

customerUserAgent.description: The buyer's User-Agent at checkout, for the same case. Flowsery keeps the browser, OS and device it resolves from it.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to act in: an id from list_workspaces. Omit to use the default workspace. Use the same workspaceId for every call about the same workspace, since ids from one workspace do not exist in another

data.description: One confirmation message once the payment is stored

tools.name: delete_payments
tools.title: Delete Payments
tools.description: Permanently delete analytics payment records, without issuing refunds or changing a payment provider. Deletes records matching every filter given (filters combine with AND): one transactionId, all payments of a visitorId, and/or a creation window. At least one of transactionId, visitorId, startAt, or endAt is required or the call fails before reaching the API; startAt and endAt are independent, so one bound alone is allowed. Without a date range, matches are deleted across the whole history. Returns the number of rows deleted. Cannot be undone and removes the revenue from every report and visitor profile, so restate website, filters, and range and get explicit confirmation first. To record a refund that already happened, use track_payment with isRefund instead. Requires websiteId or domain with a workspace token.
